extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners and PRSA members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and enforceable/non-enforceable standards from the PRSA Board of Ethics and Professional Standards for ethical practice in public relations, including core values, provisions of conduct, and topic-specific advisories (social media, AI, influencers, plagiarism, pay-for-play, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: We serve the public interest by acting as responsible advocates for those we represent. We provide a voice in the marketplace of ideas, facts, and viewpoints to aid informed public debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advocacy to support informed public debate while balancing the public interest; advocacy is a core professional value that guides behavior and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: We adhere to the highest standards of accuracy and truth in advancing the interests of those we represent and in communicating with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest and accurate in all communications; correct erroneous communications promptly; avoid deceptive practices and misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: We acquire and responsibly use specialized knowledge and experience. We advance the profession through continued professional development, research, and education. We build mutual understanding, credibility, and relationships among a wide array of institutions and audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and pursue professional development, apply specialized knowledge responsibly, and attribute expertise appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide objective counsel to those we represent. We are accountable for our actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide objective counsel, disclose influences that could affect independence, and accept accountability for professional decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: We are faithful to those we represent, while honoring our obligation to serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance duty to clients/employers with obligations to the public interest; avoid actions that betray client trust or public welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: We deal fairly with clients, employers, competitors, peers, vendors, the media, and the general public. We respect all opinions and support the right of free expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in practices that respect competitors and stakeholders; avoid unfair competitive tactics and respect free expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free Flow of Information (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Protecting and advancing the free flow of accurate and truthful information is essential to serving the public interest and contributing to informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: maintain integrity of relationships with media, government officials, and public; aid informed decision-making. Guidelines: preserve the integrity of communication processes; be honest and accurate; act promptly to correct erroneous communications for which the practitioner is responsible; preserve free flow when giving/receiving gifts by ensuring gifts are nominal, legal, and infrequent. Examples of improper conduct (e.g., giving expensive gifts to influence coverage; unlawful entertainment of officials) are provided as anti-patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Promoting healthy and fair competition among professionals preserves an ethical climate while fostering a robust business environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: promote respect and fair competition, serve public interest by providing practitioner choices. Guidelines: follow ethical hiring practices that respect free and open competition without undermining competitors; preserve intellectual property rights. Examples: sharing privileged competitive information or spreading malicious rumors are improper conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Open communication fosters informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: build trust by revealing information needed for responsible decision-making. Guidelines: be honest and accurate; act promptly to correct errors; investigate truthfulness and accuracy of released information; reveal sponsors for causes and interests; disclose financial interests (e.g., stock ownership); avoid deceptive practices. Examples include front groups, lying by omission, and failing to correct inaccurate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Confidences (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Client trust requires appropriate protection of confidential and private information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: protect privacy rights of clients, organizations, and individuals. Guidelines: safeguard confidences and privacy rights of present, former, and prospective clients and employees; protect privileged, confidential, or insider information; immediately advise appropriate authority if confidential information is being divulged by an employee. Examples include taking confidential information to a new job or intentionally leaking proprietary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Avoiding real, potential or perceived conflicts of interest builds the trust of clients, employers, and the publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: earn trust and mutual respect with clients/employers and public. Guidelines: act in the best interests of the client or employer (even subordinating personal interests); avoid actions that may appear to compromise judgment; disclose promptly any existing or potential conflict to affected clients or organizations; encourage clients to determine if a conflict exists after notification. Examples include failing to disclose financial interests in a competitor or representing conflicting interests without informing a prospective client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing the Profession (Code Provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Public relations professionals work constantly to strengthen the public’s trust in the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: build respect and credibility and improve/adapt professional practices. Guidelines: acknowledge obligation to protect and enhance the profession; keep informed and educated; pursue personal professional development; decline representation that urges actions contrary to the Code; accurately define PR capabilities; counsel subordinates in ethical decision-making; require subordinate adherence; report noncompliant practices to appropriate authority. Examples include making unsupported safety claims or assigning questionable work to non-members to avoid obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS issues Ethical Standards Advisories to provide guidance within the framework of the Code; ESAs are informational and not legal advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ESAs as interpretive guidance for emerging issues (e.g., ESA on misinformation, advisories on social media, native advertising). ESAs list applicable Code provisions and recommended practices; they are to inform member behavior and counseling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay-for-Play / "Pay-for-Play" Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS position: pay-for-play (payments for placement/coverage without disclosure) conflicts with PRSA Code provisions and deceives consumers by hiding that content was not selected on merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to avoid: request and include disclosure with final information product when compensation was provided for exposure; encourage recipients (journalists, bloggers, influencers) to disclose free or special travel, lodging, gifts or non-monetary compensation; ensure disclosures are clear and obvious so consumers can make informed decisions. Identified violations: undermines Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics & Social Media
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS position: practitioners must incorporate a higher standard of practice in social media by adhering to the PRSA Code of Ethics across platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant Code provisions: Disclosure of Information, Safeguarding Confidences, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Guidance includes: disclose paid placements and all associations with a product; protect confidential information (risk of improper disclosure via social channels); be aware of employee free-speech rights (NLRB); disclose conflicts of interest when communicating; ensure FTC-style influencer disclosures when providing samples; if gifts are given ensure they are nominal, legal and infrequent. Social media tactics should educate publics, share best practices, and maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS position: both intentional and inadvertent plagiarism are violations of ethical standards and carry equal weight; plagiarism is the unauthorized use or close imitation of another’s language and thoughts and representing them as one’s own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to avoid: do not copy content (sentence, paragraph, document) even if edited; use your own words and paraphrase (and give credit); when paraphrasing credit the original creator; use quotation marks and credit the source when copying exact wording; when using Internet sources be aware content was created by someone else and require proper credit/attribution; disclose all sources. Plagiarism implicates Free Flow of Information, Competition, Disclosure of Information, and Conflicts of Interest, and undermines honesty, expertise, and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid Spokepersons and Influencers
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS position: anyone paid to serve as a spokesperson, advocate or influencer must disclose the contractual arrangement or relationship with the sponsor of the compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable Code provisions: Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: disclose commercial relationships in advance of or simultaneous to the public forum; every party in the contractual relationship has an obligation to disclose; failure to disclose is improper conduct. Be honest and accurate in revealing sponsors and any financial interests related to outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing Front Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS position: efforts to deceive the public by creating or assisting front groups that misrepresent their mission are clear violations of the Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable provisions: Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendation: avoid assisting front groups or individuals representing undisclosed sponsorships or deceptive descriptions of goals, sponsors or participants, even if activities are lawful; prioritize transparency and open communication for informed decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overstating Fees or Compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS position: charging clients for work not performed or overstating fees and related support data is unethical and harms the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: members must charge only for services rendered and in accordance with contracts; properly report services rendered, time spent, out-of-pocket charges and related fees. Such conduct violates the obligation to enhance the profession and undermines honesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Advertising & Sponsored Content
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS position: a clear distinction between organic content and sponsored content must be made apparent to the consumer; sponsors should be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable provisions include Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Competition, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: ensure sponsorship of content is fully disclosed within the context and made consistently clear to consumers; disclosures should be clear and appropriate to the medium; sponsored content must be easily discernable from organic content and not attempt to deceive consumers; disclosures should effectively differentiate paid from organic content.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and Leadership Accountabilities (Machine Learning Accountabilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS position: when machines make decisions, accountability should rest with human beings with oversight responsibility at the time of the decision; machines cannot be assigned ultimate accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable provisions: Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: counsel senior leadership that AI cannot be held accountable for decisions; draw clear lines of human responsibility and present them forthrightly; those with oversight should identify root causes, corrective actions, and act transparently to protect the common good and ensure ethical AI operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media as a Reflection of Majority Opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS position: social media activity is not a scientifically vetted indicator of majority public opinion and may be driven by a small active minority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: communicators should not presume social media reflects majority opinion; when sharing analysis derived from social platforms, remind audiences that such sources are informal and may not accurately represent general public sentiment; cite limitations and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS position: members should refrain from leaking information to media or stakeholders without expressed approval of organizational leadership; leaking undermines trust and may be illegal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable provisions: Safeguarding Confidences, Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: be aware of laws, regulations, contracts, and employment terms that govern information flow; adhere to contractual and legal obligations; do not share confidential information obtained in trust; follow standing procedures for approved disclosure; recognize leaking can carry criminal or civil penalties.
